newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big buyer of Nike puts seen.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big buyer of Nike puts seen.

text.p: An investor was busy buying Nike Inc puts Thursday amid signs the shares may be poised to break lower, traders said.
"A large customer has been buying puts and selling calls," said a market maker at the Pacific Exchange, where Nike options trade. "They're buying a lot of July 60 and June 60 puts.
"It looks like the stock is going down considerably the way the paper's trading," he added.
In late action, Nike was down 1-1/8 at 55-3/4 on turnover of more than three million shares.
Among the options, the July 55 put traded more than 3,300 contracts, the July 60 put traded about 2,040 and the June 60 put traded 1,840. The June 55 put traded 1,125.
The most active Nike call was the July 60, with volume of nearly 2,300 contracts.
The market maker at the PCX said volatilities were up a bit but that some of the combinations that crossed were volatility neutral.
"They're buying more puts than selling calls," he said.
Implied volatilities in the July series were generally in the 40 to 50 region, traders said.
Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at Everen Securities, said support for Nike shares lies in the low- to mid-50 region, with major support in the upper 40's.
"It's a toppy-looking chart," he said, noting that the shares are below their 50-day and 200-day moving averages.
"It's a deteriorating pattern, under the moving averages, looking toppy and a bit on the shaky side," he said.
He added that if the shares recover, short-term resistance at 60 could limit any upside.
In other trading, Gateway 2000 Inc drew fairly heavy options activity on the stock's first day of trading on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock previously traded on the Nasdaq stock market.
In late trade, Gateway shares were down 1/2 at 68-3/4 after having traded between 67-1/4 and 70-1/2. Roughly 2.6 million shares changed hands.

"Today it opened up a little solid but sold off ever since. I think it's just giving back some of its gains seen in the last week," said Mike Coghlan, a designated primary market maker at TFM Investment Group in Chicago.

Coghlan said the highlight in Gateway options was a zero-cost collar done with the June 65 puts and June 75 calls, which traded about 2,960 and 2,350 contracts, respectively, on the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
A zero-cost collar is typically done by selling one option and using the proceeds to buy another.
"They bought June 65 puts and sold June 75 calls," Coghlan said.
Gateway options trade on the CBOE, the American Stock Exchange and the PCX.
